In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of high-dose chemotherapy in 3 breast cancer patients.
the application of high-dose chemotherapy in the treatment of breast cancer.
the application of the preoperative high-dose chemotherapeutic regimen with peripheral blood stem-cell transplantation in the treatment of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high-dose chemotherapy is a viable treatment option for breast cancer patients who have a high risk of developing distant metastases.
the use of preoperative chemotherapy with high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell support (HDCT-ASCS) in the treatment of primary breast cancer (BC) is still investigational.
the use of the preoperative HDT with PBSC support in breast cancer is a safe procedure, with a high response rate and an acceptable toxicity profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preoperative high-dose chemo therapy with peripheral blood stem cells support in breast cancer patients was safe and feasible.
the preoperative high-dose therapy and stem cell support (HDT/ASCT) is feasible and effective in the treatment of breast cancer patients.
the preoperative high dose chemotherapy (HD-CT) is an effective treatment for patients with locally advanced breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of high-dose chemotherapy in breast cancer is not associated with improved outcomes.
the use of high-dose chemotherapy (HDC) in the adjuvant setting for breast cancer is not justified.
the use of preoperative high-dose chemotherapies with peripheral blood stem-cell support is feasible in the treatment of patients with locally advanced breast cancer.
